items.answer:
I'll check the project's current state first, so I'm not just going from memory.Nothing was lost when you hit the limit. The last time I checked, the app built, its tests passed, and Craft Anything's check said it would pass. Today I could only look at files, not rebuild, so I can't confirm it still builds right now.

Here is what's done:

  - The Markdown preview, both split and live in your browser.
  - Sublime language packages (208 of 209 load) and a language-server connection.

The limit hit while I was building that menu work. I finished it afterwards, and the leftovers are small:

and for changing setings again settings window something like vscode or zed editor have but way simpler for any settings that can be changed and keybinds editor can be separate option and open as section in settings window and be available if settings is opened or just keybinds so we dont create two separate windows

items.answer:
I'll check the syntax question first, since it's a fact I can look up rather than a design choice. I'm comparing what Sublime has installed (including the packages you added) with what the editor loads and shows in the chooser.Shell and edit tools aren't available this session, so I can only read files. That's enough to answer the syntax question, so I'm looking at what's in your Sublime folders.Nothing in the app changed this turn. My shell and editing tools were switched off, so I could only read files. That was enough to look into the syntax question and to sketch the settings and keybinds design.

## Missing syntaxes

I can't tell you exactly which ones are missing yet, because I couldn't run the editor this turn. What I could check:

- **What you added to Sublime:** the only language packages you installed are MarkdownEditing, PowerShell and a Markdown override. The others (Nord, Catppuccin, the three Color Highlight packages, ImageMagick, MarkdownPreview, Package Control) bring colors or plugins, not languages. You also have no loose package folders.
- **What loaded earlier:** 208 of Sublime's 209 language files loaded, including your added ones. The one that failed was ActionScript, and the editor's built-in ActionScript covers it.
- **A real inconsistency:** the status-bar syntax chooser, the View ▸ Syntax menu and the Set Syntax palette use three different filters. The chooser hides any name containing "(for " or "Embedded", and the other two don't. Sublime also groups variants into submenus, so its list looks different from my flat one.

To find the exact gaps, tell me which names you expected and didn't see. Or I add an "Export syntax report" button that writes a text file comparing what Sublime lists with what the editor shows. I'd also make all three lists use the same filter.

## Settings window with keybinds inside

I'd build one window, opened by Preferences ▸ Settings (Ctrl+,). It would have a left list of sections and a search box at the top, and every change would apply instantly. Preferences ▸ Key Bindings would open the same window already on the keybinds section, so there's never a second window.

- **Sections:**
  - Appearance (the current Theme & Appearance window folds in here)
  - Editor
  - Colorizer
  - Markdown
  - Packages and Languages
  - Language Servers
  - Key Bindings
- **Keybinds editor:**
  - A searchable table of every command with its keys.
  - Click a keys cell, press the new keys, and it also takes two-step ones like Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U.
  - If the keys are already used, it names the other command and asks you to replace or cancel.
  - Reset a single row or all of them.
  - Only your changes are saved, the way Sublime's user keymap works.
- **First step:** shortcuts are currently written out by hand in three places (the key handler, the menu labels, the Markdown key list), so I'd make one command table that all three read from. Without that, a rebinding would not show up in the menus.

I found two things on your PC that suggest an import button:
- Your Sublime keymap has just two custom binds, Alt+Shift+Up/Down for Add Previous/Next Line. That's why your menu screenshots showed them.
- Your Sublime settings use JetBrains Mono 13, the "rsms dark" scheme, square tabs, one pixel of extra line padding below, and no current-line highlight.

Questions for you:
1. Should I add one-click "Import from Sublime" for those keybinds and settings?
2. Is the section list right, or do you want something removed or added?
3. Should I start with the syntax report and filter fix (quick), or with the settings and keybinds window?
